newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico industry head warns on anti-inflation zeal.
newsitem.headline: Mexico industry head warns on anti-inflation zeal.

text.p: The long-running battle against inflation in Mexico is choking an economic recovery, a top Mexican business leader said on Tuesday.

"Inflation is never a good thing, but it is not the worst enemy either," said Armando Garza Sada, president of the influential Chamber of Manufacturing Industry, which has 4,200 members in the northern Mexican industrial state of Nuevo Leon.

"This phobia with inflation that Banco de Mexico has will keep us in this situation of scant, but not necessarily sustainable growth," he told a news conference. "The worst enemy we have is this recession we are living in."
Garza proposed that the government should overcome the recession by changing the order of its priorities in economic policy.
"Controlling inflation and then seeing if we grow is not the same as trying to grow and then keeping inflation as low as possible," he added.
Garza said that inflation for the year to August was as low as 18.5 percent because the government has sought to keep it down.
Nonetheless, "the cost of having low inflation has also been high," he added.
